claim_verdicts.evidence: best-practices.md: 'Avoid overly large single widgets with a large `build()` function. Split them into different widgets based on encapsulation but also on how they change'. Note: the lesson text never actually states this claim (no mention of Flutter's docs), so the ledger entry has no sentence to anchor.

'One reason to change' and 'constructor parameters are its contract' are fine as framing. But the lesson extends it to 'everything the widget depends on' (§3) and 'nothing else reaches it' (§4). StatelessWidget doc: useful when the UI 'does not depend on anything other than the configuration information in the object itself and the [BuildContext] in which the widget is inflated.' ListTile.build starts with 'assert(debugCheckHasMaterial(context));'.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A widget's constructor parameters are its contract: everything a user of the widget must give it. The rest it needs, like the theme, it finds through its context from widgets above it.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and wrong: a widget also depends on what it looks up through its BuildContext (StatelessWidget doc: 'configuration information in the object itself and the [BuildContext] in which the widget is inflated'). The inline ListTile needs a Material ancestor: ListTile.build asserts debugCheckHasMaterial. A scratch test pumping ProductTile(product: p) with no Material above it threw 'No Material widget found.' So 'or in a test' with only a product is false. The prereq stateless-vs-stateful teaches the context dependency.
issues.quote: What an extracted widget needs is written in its constructor, and nothing else reaches it.
issues.fix: Replace with: "What an extracted widget needs from its caller is written in its constructor. The rest, like the theme, it finds through its context from the widgets above it." In the next sentences change "or in a test" to "or in a test inside a MaterialApp". In §3 change the contract definition from "everything the widget depends on" to "everything its caller must give it".

issues.text: Unlisted claim (same issue as §4): the definition says the constructor lists 'everything the widget depends on', which ignores what the widget gets through its BuildContext (theme, Material ancestor).
issues.quote: everything a user of the widget must give it, and everything the widget depends on.
issues.fix: Change to: "widget contract — the constructor parameters of a widget: everything a user of the widget must give it."

issues.text: Unlisted claim (behavior) not in the ledger. It is supportable: best-practices.md 'When `setState()` is called on a `State` object, all descendent widgets rebuild' and setState doc 'causes the framework to schedule a [build] for this [State] object'. But it must be in claims.
issues.quote: a `setState` in it rebuilds only its own subtree.
issues.fix: Add a claim (kind behavior, version_key flutter) with source_hint refs/flutter-website perf/best-practices.md:59-60 and Flutter SDK framework.dart:1066-1069 (State.setState doc). No text change needed.

issues.text: Prose does not match the code. DonHangApp.build constructs only ProductListScreen (main.dart:21). LoginScreen is constructed in product_list_screen.dart:38 and CreateOrderScreen in login_screen.dart:32, both through Navigator. §5 body gets this right ('only sets up the app and names its first screen'). The summary line contradicts it.
issues.quote: `DonHangApp` composes the app from one widget per screen, each requiring only an `ApiClient`.
issues.fix: Replace summary line 2 with: "The app is composed of one widget per screen, each requiring only an `ApiClient`; `DonHangApp` only sets up the app and names the first one."

issues.text: Key (a) is right, but the explanation repeats the false 'nothing else reaches it' (see §4 issue). q2's correct explanation 'can be reused wherever a product exists' has the same overreach, because the row also needs a Material ancestor.
issues.quote: The constructor lists everything the widget depends on; nothing else reaches it.
issues.fix: q1 correct (en): "The constructor lists everything a caller must give the widget." (vi): "Constructor liệt kê mọi thứ bên gọi phải đưa cho widget." q2 correct: replace "so it can be reused wherever a product exists" with "so it can be reused on any screen that has a product" (vi tương ứng).

issues.text: Overstated. ProductListScreen imports login_screen.dart and constructs LoginScreen(apiClient: ...) (line 38), and LoginScreen constructs CreateOrderScreen (line 32). So each knows the next screen's constructor, though not its build.
issues.quote: None of them knows how the others are built.
issues.fix: Change to: "None of them depends on how the others build their UI; a screen that opens another only calls its constructor."

issues.text: In this code build does not load products: fetchProducts() is called in initState (product_list_screen.dart:23) and _reload (27). build only shows the progress indicator, error, empty and list states from the future.
issues.quote: in the middle of the code that loads products, shows the loading indicator, handles errors and draws the title bar
issues.fix: Change to "in the middle of the code that waits for the products, shows the loading indicator, handles errors and draws the title bar". In §4 change "A screen's `build` method that loads data" to "A screen whose `build` method waits for data".

The Suggested answer's 'keep and replace the `_products` load' also depends on _reload working.
issues.quote: lines=56-65
issues.fix: No text change now. When the _reload fix lands at stage-1, re-run tools/extract-code DonHang.App/lib/screens/product_list_screen.dart --tag stage-1 and update the `lines=` range. Then re-validate.

issues.text: This paragraph jumps: no example in the lesson shows a small widget holding its own state, and 'When one of them changes' is ambiguous (its code changes, or its state?). Summary line 5 rests on this paragraph, so I cannot reconstruct why extracting keeps state 'in the right place'.
